Title: Diagnosis of test `testGenerateURLFragment`
Details: The test `testGenerateURLFragment` checks whether HTML entities such as `"` are correctly escaped to their corresponding character by the `StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment` method. However, the test failure indicates that this is not the case. Consequently, un-escaped strings are being returned, which leads to the error demonstrated by the test.

Title: Diagnosis of test `testSoftLineBreakEncode`
Details: The test `testSoftLineBreakEncode` expects that encoding the string `expected` using `QuotedPrintableCodec.encode(String)` will produce the string `qpdata`, which contains a quoted-printable soft line break `b=\r\neautiful` and an encoded '=' character as `=3D`.

From the code:
1. `QuotedPrintableCodec.encode(String)` calls `encode(String, String)` with the default charset.
2. `encode(String, String)` converts the input string to bytes in the given charset and calls `encode(byte[])`.
3. `encode(byte[])` calls `encodeQuotedPrintable(PRINTABLE_CHARS, bytes)`.
4. `encodeQuotedPrintable(BitSet, byte[])` encodes the byte array using quoted-printable rules.
5. For each byte, if the byte is printable, it's written as-is, otherwise it is encoded as `=XX` via `encodeQuotedPrintable(int, ByteArrayOutputStream)`.

However, in the test, the string `expected` does not contain the literal `=3D` but only the character '='. The test expects that encoding will insert this explicit encoded `=3D` and also include the soft line break represented by `b=\r\neautiful`.

The current `encodeQuotedPrintable` implementation seemingly does not insert soft line breaks in the output, it only encodes non-printable characters. The test expects soft line breaks to be inserted, but the implementation doesn't add any.

Because of that, when the test calls `qpcodec.encode(expected)`, it returns a string without the expected soft line break and without encoding the '=' character as `=3D`, causing the test to fail.

Hence, the root cause is that the encoding method doesn't handle encoding of '=' character or insertion of soft line breaks as per quoted-printable encoding rules.

Suggested methods to fix include those involved in encoding the string to quoted-printable bytes, especially where encoding decisions for special characters and line breaks happen.

Proposed fix locations:
org.apache.commons.codec.net.QuotedPrintableCodec.encodeQuotedPrintable(java.util.BitSet,byte[])
org.apache.commons.codec.net.QuotedPrintableCodec.encodeQuotedPrintable(int,java.io.ByteArrayOutputStream)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
